evidence: The survivor explicitly says "try colors 1..3 in order for lexicographic minimality"; its code treats each constraint as an adjacency conflict. The failed greedy solution likewise assigns colors from "(1, 2, 3)" while checking adjacent colors.
affordance_in_statement: You are tasked with finding an integer sequence c_1, c_2, ..., c_n where each element must be chosen from the set {1, 2, 3}. ... every given pair must satisfy ... gcd(c_u, c_v) < lcm(c_u, c_v)
removal_suggestion: This is intrinsic to the stated task: for values restricted to {1,2,3}, the gcd/lcm inequality is exactly c_u != c_v, so the problem is inherently 3-coloring. It cannot be removed without changing the task. If only presentation may change, avoid exposing the condition as a direct pairwise compatibility test; present the same requirement indirectly through a compatibility relation or scenario.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes each constraint as a color conflict and performs depth-first assignment in value order, relying on the first complete assignment being lexicographically smallest.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: each element must be chosen from the set {1, 2, 3}; every given pair must satisfy gcd(c_u, c_v) < lcm(c_u, c_v); determine the lexicographically smallest valid sequence

common_affordance: The gcd/lcm condition over the fixed domain {1,2,3} reduces every constraint to requiring unequal endpoint values, i.e. ordinary 3-coloring with colors tried in lexicographic order.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It uses greedy coloring without backtracking. A locally available smallest color need not permit a completion, and it does not establish lexicographic optimality globally.
It relies on exhaustive recursive search over assignments, which can take exponential time on hard 3-coloring instances despite the n <= 40 bound.
It likewise uses brute-force/backtracking search for the coloring problem and times out on adversarial instances.

recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can reliably defeat the survivor: the reduction to 3-coloring is the structural core of the task. If a presentation-only change is required, replace the conspicuous gcd/lcm inequality with an indirect compatibility rule in the scenario, without stating that compatible pairs are simply unequal.
